children: The relevance harness that keeps Search honest — MRR and NDCG@10 over JSONL fixtures, scored the same way for both engines.
Golden Eval is a reproducible relevance harness. It runs a fixed set of queries against Search and scores the returned rankings with two standard information-retrieval metrics:
(Mean Reciprocal Rank) — how high the first relevant result lands.
(Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at 10) — graded relevance across the top ten, discounted by position.

fixtures: each line pairs a query with its expected-relevant Documents. The fixtures are the "golden" set — they make a relevance change measurable instead of anecdotal, so a tweak to the Search Vector weights or to BM25F field weights can be accepted or rejected on numbers.

Barkpark runs two engines behind one contract, and Golden Eval is how their trade-offs are quantified: the same fixtures score Postgres Search (ts_rank over the Search Vector, pg_trgm widen) and the Indx Engine (BM25F ranking) side by side. It also catches regressions from upstream query rewrites — a bad Synonyms row promoted by the Auto Correction Loop, or a noisy Did You Mean suggestion — before they reach the Web Demo. Any learned re-ranking trained on the Search Intelligence clickstream is validated against this same golden set before it ships. The harness is the rigor layer beneath the whole search story in Barkpark.
